title: Impact of Microfinance Branch Entry on Household Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)

• The dataset has a clear treated × post interaction (treat_x_post) that isolates households located in areas where a micro-finance branch has just entered (“treated”) and in the period after the entry (“post”).  
• We exploit the before/after contrast within treated households and compare it to the same time contrast in control households.  

Key identifying assumption: Parallel trends  
In the absence of branch entry, the change in log-consumption for treated households would have followed the same average evolution as that of control households. We will:

1. Include household (unit) fixed effects to absorb time-invariant heterogeneity.  
2. Include period fixed effects to absorb aggregate shocks.  
3. Cluster standard errors at the household level.  
4. Conduct placebo and alternative-specification robustness checks to gauge the plausibility of the parallel-trends assumption.

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Impact of Microfinance Branch Entry on Household Consumption
# Difference-in-Differences with robustness checks
############################################################

# Install/load required packages
required_pkgs <- c("readr", "dplyr", "fixest", "broom")
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for(p in required_pkgs) if(!(p %in% installed)) install.packages(p)
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(fixest); library(broom)

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s39_data.csv"
df <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Ensure correct types
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(across(c(unit_id, period, treated, post, treat_x_post), as.integer))

# 2. Baseline DID with two-way fixed effects -------------------------------
did_base <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data = df, cluster = ~unit_id
)

cat("\n================= Baseline DID Result =================\n")
print(etable(did_base, se = "cluster"))

# Extract and display coefficient & 95% CI
coefs <- broom::tidy(did_base, conf.int = TRUE)
did_coef <- coefs %>% filter(term == "treat_x_post")
cat("\nEstimated treatment effect (log points):\n")
print(did_coef)

# 3. Robustness check A: Simple DID without FE -----------------------------
did_simple <- feols(
  y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post,
  data = df, cluster = ~unit_id
)

cat("\n============= Robustness A: Simple DID (no FE) =============\n")
print(etable(did_simple, se = "cluster"))

# 4. Robustness check B: Placebo test on pre-periods only -------------------
# Keep only pre-period observations and create a fake post variable
pre_df <- df %>% filter(post == 0) %>%
  mutate(fake_post = ifelse(period == min(period), 0, 1),
         fake_treat_post = treated * fake_post)

placebo <- feols(
  y ~ fake_treat_post | unit_id + period,
  data = pre_df, cluster = ~unit_id
)

cat("\n============= Robustness B: Placebo (pre-period only) =============\n")
print(etable(placebo, se = "cluster"))

# 5. Robustness check C: Allow for differential linear trends --------------
# If >2 periods, interact treated with period to soak up different linear trends
if(length(unique(df$period)) > 2){
  df <- df %>% mutate(trend = as.numeric(scale(period)))
  did_trend <- feols(
    y ~ treat_x_post + treated:trend | unit_id + period,
    data = df, cluster = ~unit_id
  )
  cat("\n============= Robustness C: DID with unit-specific trends =============\n")
  print(etable(did_trend, se = "cluster"))
}

############################################################
# End of analysis
############################################################
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive.  
Magnitude: roughly +0.12 to +0.25 log points (≈ 12 %–25 %) increase in consumption for households gaining microfinance access versus controls.  

Rationale: Prior micro-finance impact studies generally find modest but significant improvements in household consumption (especially smoothing of shocks) once credit constraints are relaxed. Given the short time horizon implied by the data (two or a few periods) and the fact that most households are micro-entrepreneurs, a 10-25 % bump in consumption is plausible while still leaving room for heterogeneity.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in household consumption before and after microfinance branch entry between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The entry of a microfinance branch is associated with a positive effect on household consumption.
_ground_truth.main_effect: Approximately 0.15 increase in log household consumption.
